question: A 30-year-old primigravida schedules an appointment with her obstetrician for a regular check-up. She says that everything is fine, although she reports that her baby has stopped moving as much as previously. She is 22 weeks gestation. She denies any pain or vaginal bleeding. The obstetrician performs an ultrasound and also orders routine blood and urine tests. On ultrasound, there is no fetal cardiac activity or movement. The patient is asked to wait for 1 hour, after which the scan is to be repeated. The second scan shows the same findings. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
analysis: The patient is 22 weeks pregnant and reports decreased fetal movement. The ultrasound shows no fetal cardiac activity or movement on two separate occasions, indicating that the fetus has died. This condition is referred to as fetal demise, which is the loss of a fetus after 20 weeks of gestation. Other options such as missed abortion, incomplete abortion, and complete abortion are not applicable here as they typically refer to earlier gestational ages or different clinical scenarios. Ectopic pregnancy is also ruled out as it occurs outside the uterus and would not present with a viable intrauterine pregnancy at this stage.
